Golf ranked as the 7th most popular sport in the United States in 2020. My hot take is that golf is more fun than people realize and will get into either the 4th or 5th spot in the next 5-10 years, because people are starting to see the fun of golf. Often, golf as a sport (or activity depending on if you want to devalue it as a sport) is marred by the country club perception and the fact it's not all that exciting to watch on TV. But the beautiful thing about golf is that when you go out there, you can play by whatever rules you want. If you're matched up with strangers, maybe communicate if you're going to do something out of the ordinary, but a majority of people don't care as long as you don't stop them from having a good time and don't act like a child. Don't feel like keeping score? Don't! Want to tee the ball up in the middle of the fairway and hit Driver every time? It's your experience, do what you want (safely)! Feel like moving your ball so you're not in the sand or behind a tree? Go for it! Those in charge are realizing that there's much more money to be made being inclusive (which is a sentence that really applies to every industry after 2020), so smart golf courses and experiences like Top Golf realize that it's more about having fun. And people are realizing that there is fun to be had that they didn't realize before. Golf on TV still has a long way to go, but they're starting to catch up to the idea that entertaining the audience is more important than keeping up with country club norms, as evidenced by the golf matches that have paired up celebrities and non-golf athletes with the best golfers in the world. By 2030, golf will have overtaken tennis, hockey, and maybe even soccer in terms of overall popularity. (For clarification, I have soccer passing hockey for the 4th spot in the next 10 years, as well)

We've reached the point in human history where something new from a subjectively judged medium like art/entertainment can no longer become the "Greatest of All Time".  From 1939 to 1941, "Gone with the Wind" was the greatest movie of all time, until "Citizen Kane" came around to claim that title.  In 1972, "The Godfather" staked its claim as the GOAT.  Were those movies really the greatest thing ever created, or were they the best because there were only 10 good movies out at the time?  We've reached a point now where we have such an incredibly vast existence of movies/TV shows/music/art, that nothing new can ever overcome the decades/centuries of its predecessors.  Let's say an artist painted an absolute masterpiece tomorrow, the likes of which has never been seen.  Would the world deem it better than the Mona Lisa?  Of course not.  Can anything new from a subjectively judged medium like arts/entertainment become the new GOAT?  Nope.

Salads are the greatest meal, and anyone who disagrees is making them incorrectly. Look I get it - a salad can never compare to a chocolate bar or mac & cheese. But for your average day to day meal, salads are superior. 
1) Good for you. If you're pouring a half bottle of ranch over a head of iceberg lettuce you're doing it wrong. Salads should be healthy AND delicious. You can throw so many vegetables in a bowl and cover with your favourite dressing. Boom, vitamins.
2) Volume. Sometimes you want to shove as much food inside of you as possible. Salads are perfect for that. Chop a head of lettuce and add any vegetables you have and put cheese on top. Make the biggest bowl of salad you could ever want. You won't feel like a pile of garbage after eating it but you'll be so satisfied.
3) Versatility. There's only so many different kinds of burgers you can have and it still tastes 75% like bread and beef. The only thing that remains constant in a salad is the dressing. There are hundreds of kinds of dressing! Don't like some veggies? Don't use them! Throw some of every vegetable you like in a salad bowl. It's probably going to taste good together. Or get crazy and throw some fruit in there! Mix it up and make a peanut sauce dressing! There's salads that taste like cheeseburgers. The possibilities are endless.
4) Texture. Sure mac & cheese is great, but you're eating a pile of mush. Salad is CRUNCHY. But then also creamy with the dressing. Chewy if you add raising. Bigger crunch if you add croutons. Soft if you add mango. It's a party for your teeth in every bowl.
5) The definition of salad is expanding. Maybe you're not a leafy green kind of person. Pasta salad! Potato salad! Quinoa salad! Bean salad! Put it in a bowl and add dressing and you have a delicious salad with myriad flavours that you could have for any meal. I'm even prepared to pitch the idea of breakfast salad.
